reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses corrosion of high-entropy alloys in fluoride salts and aqueous solutions, focusing on elemental dissolution and thermodynamic stability, with no mention of Q235 steel, native iron oxide layers, or the proposed thermal degradation mechanism. The key premises are entirely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: A native iron oxide layer (Fe3O4) on Q235 steel acts as a protective barrier at room temperature.
High-temperature exposure (700–900 °C) causes grain coarsening, thermal stresses, and microcracking in the oxide scale.
Microstructural degradation of the oxide scale leads to spallation and elevated mass loss in aggressive salt environments.
The corrosion mechanism is governed by the integrity and adherence of the native oxide scale, not by alloying elements.
